title: The Holiness of God
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The holiness of God means that God is utterly set apart in purity, glory, majesty, and moral perfection. He is not common, corrupt, compromised, or like sinful humanity.
summary: The holiness of God means that God is utterly set apart in purity, glory, majesty, and moral perfection. He is not common, corrupt, compromised, or like sinful humanity.
christFocus: Jesus Christ reveals the holiness of God in human flesh. He is without sin, perfectly obedient, pure in heart, and worthy of worship. At the cross, God’s holiness is not ignored, but upheld as Christ gives Himself to save sinners.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
God’s holiness means He is completely set apart from all that is sinful, false, impure, and unworthy. He is not merely better than creation; He is in a category of His own. His glory, purity, beauty, and moral perfection are unmatched.

When Isaiah saw the Lord high and lifted up, the cry of heaven was “Holy, holy, holy.” The vision did not make Isaiah casual or self-confident. It exposed his uncleanness and his need for mercy. God’s holiness reveals both His majesty and humanity’s sinfulness.

God’s holiness also shapes His people. Because He is holy, His people are called to be holy. Holiness is not self-righteousness, isolation, or religious performance. It is belonging to God and being set apart for His worship, truth, purity, and obedience.

The holiness of God makes the Gospel shine more brightly. Sin is not small, and grace is not cheap. Christ came to cleanse unholy sinners, bring them near to God, and form them into a holy people who reflect His character.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People often treat God as though He is common, casual, adjustable, or safe to approach on human terms. The holiness of God corrects shallow worship, careless sin, and a reduced view of grace. God is near to His people, but He is never ordinary.

This doctrine also helps the ashamed and broken understand the wonder of mercy. God does not save sinners because sin is minor. He saves through Christ because His holiness is real and His grace is greater than our uncleanness. The holy God does not merely tolerate His people; He cleanses them and makes them His own.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Approach God with reverence, humility, and gratitude. Do not make peace with sin or treat grace as permission to remain unchanged. Let God’s holiness lead you to worship, confession, purity, obedience, and deeper dependence on Christ, who alone makes unholy people clean before God.
